ROUTE_IDENTITY.finding: The single route key obligation:track-only:MA:ma-bmc-multi agrees across source-receipt.json, production-field-map.json, the MASTER_QUEUE row (routeCount 1) and the packet-set manifest, and is printed on both delivered pages. The relief and its authority are on the delivered face: 'CONSOLIDATED PETITION TO SEAL MULTIPLE CRIMINAL RECORDS UNDER G.L. c. 276, Sec. 100C AND BMC AMENDED STANDING ORDER No. 1-09', with Commonwealth v. Pon, 469 Mass. 296 (2014) cited for the good-cause standard — the same three authorities the receipt declares.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.finding: Measured against the mounted corpus and the committed records. The MASTER_QUEUE row records boundCount 0, officialFormFamily NONE, forms [] and the receipt's zero-binary claim matches exactly. Both grounding records exist and say what is cited. I then tested the harder claim — that composing a custom petition here is authorised rather than invented — against two held sources: the corpus MA legal review (ASOF 2026-07-30) Track 8, which records 'Is an official form mandatory? Unresolved ... whether BMC publishes a form was not established'; and the corpus governance file ADOPTED_BATCH_2_LEGAL_RESEARCH_RESOLUTION.md, which directs at line 129 that 'If no current BMC form is published, a counsel-approved custom consolidated petition may be used only for qualifying BMC records; otherwise use TC0057 per case'. The receipt's formIdentityNote paraphrases that resolution accurately. The two MA assets in the corpus that are forms are both EXPUNGEMENT petitions (MA-PROBATION-SERVICE under §§ 100F/100G/100H, and TC0021 for marijuana offences) — a different remedy from § 100C sealing — and are correctly not bound. No form was substituted and none was invented.

COMPONENT_SET.finding: requiredComponentsMissing 0. The packet-set manifest declares two required components — primary_filing (order 1) and instructions (order 2) — the field map declares the same two, and both delivered fixtures carry both across four pages. The corpus Track 8 component list (consolidated petition required, participant instructions required, supporting documentation conditional on the judge's request) matches. Noted for the repairer as a non-blocking improvement, not scored as a defect: the packet tells the participant the consolidated petition 'SUPPLEMENTS the statewide per-case form' without naming that form TC0057, which the held review and the Batch 2 resolution both name. The form is correctly not a component of this packet — the participant files it per case — and the packet names the clerk of the venue division as the authority on how the division wants it presented.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: knownRequiredFieldsMissing 0. Six writes owed, six made, and I read each back off the delivered bytes myself rather than trusting the report: petitioner name (in the caption 'IN THE MATTER OF THE PETITION OF ...', in paragraph 1 and at PRINTED NAME), date of birth, mailing address, telephone, email, and the instructions page's participant name. The boundary fixture carries all six in their long forms.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: requiredFactsNotCollected 0 and the six declared items are honest ones the platform genuinely cannot hold: the three record lines (division, docket number, disposition), the further-records line, the participant-authored good-cause narrative, and the venue division. Each is disclosed to the participant in participant-instructions.md with a specific instruction on what to write and where it comes from, and everyRequiredBeforeFilingItemIsDisclosed is true. I checked the classification against the delivered face and every one of the six is a real blank on the petition, correctly labelled, with no court-owned field among them. The manifest's separate obtain-document action — request your own CORI from DCJIS — is disclosed on the delivered instructions page under 'YOUR CORI FIRST', which also states the platform never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: requiredOptionsMissing 0. routeSelectionsMade is empty and no map declares a selectionControl; the packet renders no election. The one threshold that gates the route — three or more records from two or more BMC divisions — is printed at the top of the petition in capitals and walked again on the instructions page, with the instruction to count against the participant's own CORI. The venue election is left to the participant with the Standing Order's rule stated, not guessed.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: incompleteRows 0. The petition's paragraph 2 is a genuine repeating structure — Record 1, Record 2, Record 3, plus a 'Further records, if any' continuation — and every row is left uniformly blank for the participant with the same three sub-facts named in each. No row is part-filled, which is the failure mode this obligation exists to catch: there is no row carrying a docket number with an empty disposition.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: protectedWrites 0 and invisibleWrites 0, and the refusals are correctly classified. Both protected blanks — petitioner_signature and signature_date — carry refusalClass signature_or_date_participant_completion, and the delivered page states beneath them '(The petitioner signs and dates this petition personally. Nothing on this page is signed or dated for the petitioner.)'. nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes is 0 and refusedFieldsWithInk is empty on both fixtures.

ARTIFACTS.finding: I rehashed both fixtures and both match reports/rendered-artifacts.json and the RASTER_PASS receipt's bindings.

PAGE_ORDER.finding: Declared 4 pages and pdfinfo reports 4 for both fixtures. The primary_filing pages precede the instructions pages, which is the order the manifest declares (primary_filing order 1, instructions order 2), and the petition's numbered paragraphs run 1 through 5 in sequence across the break.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: visualDefects 0 on my own run, over bytes carrying a hash-bound RASTER_PASS receipt (run 33574304514) whose two hash bindings equal the hashes I computed. I additionally checked the boundary fixture, which is where clipping shows: the 99-character mailing address wraps cleanly onto a second line ending '...Dorchester, Massachusetts 02124-2214', the 60-character email prints complete, and the hyphenated apostrophised name prints complete in all three places it appears. Nothing is truncated and nothing overlaps.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: A1 test: the repository establishes the answer and the packet states it. MA.memo.json rules.filing records 'File the consolidated petition in the BMC division identified by the Standing Order's residence-based venue rule', and the corpus Track 8 records 'Filing method: Paper filing in the correct BMC division' with the venue rule keyed to residence and the fallback to the division of the most recent eligible record. The delivered packet states that rule twice — in the petition's caption instruction and again under 'THE VENUE RULE' on the instructions page — in both branches, and leaves the division blank for the participant because it turns on facts the platform does not hold.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Met on the third branch of DETERMINATION_FEE_AND_WAIVER_STANDARD. I asked first whether the repository establishes the fee: it does not. MA.memo.json records fees 'None identified in the review' and feeWaiver 'None identified', and the corpus Track 8 records 'Fee: None identified. Unresolved.' The packet states exactly that position and names the office that answers it: 'FEES. The controlling review identified no filing fee and no waiver for this route. This packet asserts neither; the clerk of the venue division can say whether anything is charged.' That is a named checkable authority — the clerk of the division the participant is filing in, an office reachable in practice — and not the 'check with the court' gesture the standard refuses. It also correctly declines to convert 'none identified' into 'no fee is charged'.

SERVICE.finding: The repository's answer is that notice here is the court's act, not the participant's, and the packet says so without inventing a participant service step. MA.memo.json rules.notice records 'Preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing per the Standing Order' and rules.service 'Per the Standing Order'; the corpus Track 8 adds that 'The Clerk-Magistrate notifies the Probation Department. Public notice of the final hearing is required' and records the exact form of that notice as an open question. The delivered instructions state 'WHAT FOLLOWS FILING. Under the Standing Order: a preliminary hearing, public notice, and a final hearing', attribute it to the Standing Order, and name the clerk of the venue division as the authority on how the division wants papers presented. Nothing unresolved is asserted as settled. Noted as a non-blocking improvement: the held review also records that the final hearing is set 30 to 45 days out and that § 100C ¶2 requires the Clerk-Magistrate to post the petition on a public bulletin board until the hearing; the packet conveys 'public notice' without those two specifics.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Present on the delivered face. The instructions page carries 'WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD OF FILING' with four stops — threshold not met, any record outside the BMC, the judge requesting additional information, and a hearing being set — and states separately that 'A hearing is where self-help stops'. That matches the corpus Track 8 self-help limits, including the stop where records span BMC and another court department, which the packet renders as 'any record is outside the Boston Municipal Court Department'.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.evidence: The route key itself agrees everywhere and occurs exactly once in the census: obligation:track-only:MA:ma-bmc-multi, in source-receipt.json, production-field-map.json, the MASTER_QUEUE row and route-obligation-candidate.json, and printed at the foot of both delivered components. What is blocked is the identity of the controlling petition, and the governing registry still refuses it in terms. data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track ma-bmc-multi, carries formIdentityInvestigation with status STOPPED_AMBIGUOUS, reviewedOn 2026-09-04, and this hardStop, quoted exactly: 'Do not assign TC0057, TC0059, or the existing custom pleading as the controlling single petition until the issuing court identifies the petition form referenced by the current Standing Order or confirms that no dedicated form is published.' That sentence names the existing custom pleading -- the very component this packet renders as primary_filing -- and forbids assigning it as the controlling single petition. The record reviewed both official candidates and rejected each: TC0057 as NOT_ESTABLISHED_AS_CONSOLIDATED_BMC_PETITION because 'The form expressly directs the filer to use a separate form for each case and carries one docket-number caption', and TC0059 as NOT_IDENTIFIED_BY_ISSUER_AS_BMC_MULTI_RECORD_PETITION. WHAT THE QUEUE SETTLED IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION. The MASTER_QUEUE row's legalInputStatus is SETTLED and its executionReclassification's nextExecutableAction reads 'Use the existing codified-text custom-pleading treatment and proceed through current raster and independent-verification gates', but the ownerDecision beside it is 'CUSTOM_PLEADING_FROM_CODIFIED_TEXT is not external source-acquisition work. Do not research or reacquire this family.' That settles the SOURCE-ACQUISITION question, and the same row still carries the laneReturnLegalHold from VF05 naming ROUTE_IDENTITY and COMPONENT_SET. The packet-set manifest names primary_filing with officialFormId null, which is consistent with the pleading being rendered but says nothing about it being controlling; the registry entry that does speak to that is the hard stop above, and it is the later record (reviewedOn 2026-09-04).
ROUTE_IDENTITY.finding: The governing registry still refuses to identify the custom pleading as the controlling single petition, and the sentence that refuses it names that pleading expressly. This obligation cannot be ruled on the bytes; it waits on the issuing court.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.evidence: THE TWO RECORDS THIS BUILD IS GROUNDED ON CARRY NO DIGEST AT ALL. source-receipt.json codifiedGrounds holds exactly two entries and each has only 'record' and 'what' -- no sha256, no byteLength, no exactObject, nothing to recompute against. The receipt's own bindingMethod says so rather than claiming otherwise: 'grounded on two committed records, verified present and un-drifted before anything is composed'. The builder confirms it: scripts/build-census-v1-ma-bmc-multi-set.mjs computes sha256 only over its own output packet bytes and over its raster PNGs, and never over MA.memo.json or legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json; the only record digest it prints anywhere is TC0057's, in prose. So nothing in this family binds its authority by exact SHA-256, and a reader cannot tell which bytes of either record the packet was composed from. For the record, the current digests are MA.memo.json c4412f8a62a9d8dc24d7da6f01ce8ac4b530a5cfc2907d66224401d2097b110a (105439) and legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json 6076f7346c41bbef18623060c8c0397bded4149e55c2e975693b0da217541eec (3683419), recomputed here -- but recomputing a digest the receipt does not carry proves nothing about the build. This is the same defect this lane raised on Nevada and that the FIX08 cluster commit repaired there by adding sha256 and byteLength to both codified-ground records; the identical repair is available here and is not a legal question.
SOURCE_IDENTITY.finding: No source binds by exact SHA-256. The defect is independent of the legal block and does not clear when the block clears; a repair lane can fix it now.

COMPONENT_SET.evidence: Physically the set is whole and I checked it on the bytes: the packet-set manifest names two components, primary_filing (order 1) and instructions (order 2), both required and both outputStrategy custom_pleading; both reach a page in both fixtures; the page manifest maps pages 1-2 to primary_filing and 3-4 to instructions; and the first printed line of each page confirms it (CONSOLIDATED PETITION TO SEAL MULTIPLE CRIMINAL RECORDS ... / the petition's paragraph-3 continuation / THRESHOLD, VENUE AND WHAT FOLLOWS FILING / WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD OF FILING). What cannot be ruled is whether that is the CORRECT controlling set, and for the same reason as ROUTE_IDENTITY: the registry's hard stop forbids assigning the existing custom pleading as the controlling single petition, and it also leaves open whether TC0057 belongs in the file alongside it. The packet is candid about exactly this: its own receipt says 'that TC0057 is or is not additionally required in the file alongside this consolidated petition' is something the receipt does not establish, and step 7 of participant-instructions.md tells the participant 'Ask before you file; do not assume this petition alone is the whole filing.' A packet that has to tell the participant it may not be the whole filing is a packet whose component set the record has not closed.
